pr_body:
Take into account possible in-flight operations that are not captured
in the commit local checkpoint but are considered as persisted during
local recovery.

Closes #79923

cc @arteam
pr_comments: Did you manage to reproduce this and if so, can you reveal instructions for how to?
With the seed in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/79923 it's quite easy to reproduce.

> With the seed in #79923 it's quite easy to reproduce.

I tried locally before my comment above and the test succeeded. It almost consistently does succeed in my intellij.

But putting load on my laptop (by running the same test in gradle), it starts failing. And it fails consistently on my CI box.

This makes me wonder if we are on the right path with the fix here. It looks more like a missing wait condition than the change made here. Perhaps you have more info (will continue looking too)?

does it fail with the same error as before? I was able to reproduce the issue consistently adding a `Thread.sleep` in `InternalEngine#commitIndexWriter` just after we set the commit user data. But maybe we're hitting something else here.
Sorry for the delay on addressing your comments @henningandersen, I've added a local checkpoint tracker to avoid the problems you mentioned in your review.

review_comments: I see the need for this now though I wonder if we could find a reasonable approximation and make the failing check below a range instead? We could use `[lcp, max]` as the range. This version is more precise though, so we can also take your route.
I think we should keep this version to avoid possible false positives. The downside is that we're replicating production logic in the test case.
